sup.2: The support button in the app brings you here. Most problems are answered below — these are the questions we actually get asked, in the order we get asked them. If yours isn't here, message us and we'll take it from there.
sup.3: Writing to us? Send these four things
sup.4: Every case that gets solved in one reply includes them, and every case that drags on is missing them:
sup.5: Your phone model and the app name and version
sup.6: For USB apps: the drive size and file system, and the adapter you're using
sup.7: Exactly what you were doing when it happened, step by step
sup.8: A screenshot of the error or the screen you're stuck on
sup.10: For purchases, refunds, business enquiries and press — anything that needs a written record.
sup.12: For quick questions and screenshots. Include the app name, your phone model, and what you were doing when it happened.
sup.16: The app says no device is connected
sup.17: Our apps talk to the drive directly over USB, so they can open drives Android itself can't, such as NTFS, ext4 or bootable drives. The phone still has to detect the drive. Work through this in order:
sup.18: Open your phone's Settings, search for OTG, and switch it on if the option exists.
sup.19: Check your adapter is a real data OTG adapter, not a charge-only cable. This is by far the most common cause.
sup.19b: When you plug the drive in, Android asks whether to let the app use the USB device. Tap OK. If you refused, unplug the drive and plug it in again. In Ultimate USB, DROFUS, Ventoy and USB Tools, also check the mode on the main screen is USB OTG, not SD Slot.
sup.20: Plug in a drive formatted as FAT32 or exFAT and check that Android notices it: most phones show a notification or a USB access prompt. Your phone's own file manager may not list NTFS or ext4 drives even when our apps can open them. If even a FAT32 drive isn't noticed, the problem is the cable, the port or the drive.
sup.21: Test the same drive on a PC to rule the drive out.
sup.22: Check the charging port for dust or lint.
sup.24: Most Android phones made in the last several years do. If searching Settings for OTG returns nothing, your phone most likely enables it automatically — the absence of a toggle isn't a sign it's unsupported. Confirm by plugging in a drive formatted as FAT32 or exFAT and checking your file manager.
sup.26: No — not for USB drives over OTG, which is what these apps are built for.
sup.27: Root is only needed to reach the phone's internal SD card slot, because Android doesn't expose it the same way. If you need to work on a microSD card without root, put it in a USB card reader and connect that over OTG instead.
sup.28: Can I use an external hard drive?
sup.29: Flash drives, card readers, portable SSDs and OTG hubs are supported. Mechanical external hard drives (HDDs) are not officially supported — they draw more power than a phone's USB port reliably provides, so they may fail to spin up or cut out mid-operation.
sup.30: If you try one anyway: charge the phone fully first, and use a powered USB hub if you have one.
sup.31: The drive disconnects part-way through an operation
sup.32: A drive that drops out mid-write is almost always a physical connection problem, not a software one:
sup.33: Don't move the phone or the cable while an operation is running — a fractionally loose adapter will disconnect on the smallest movement.
sup.34: Try a different OTG adapter. Cheap adapters fail under sustained load even when they work for a quick file copy.
sup.35: Keep the phone charged; a drive under sustained write load draws real power.
sup.36: Android says the drive is corrupted or unsupported after I format it
sup.37: That notification is expected after a drive is formatted as NTFS or ext2/3/4, and often after a bootable drive is written. It does not mean anything is wrong. Most Android devices have no built-in driver for these, so the system sees a drive it can't read and reports it as damaged or unsupported.
sup.38: The write succeeded. Our apps read and write these file systems with their own drivers, so in Ultimate USB and Ventoy the drive still opens in USB File Manager.
sup.39: Dismiss the notification and never tap the option to format — that offer comes from Android, not from us, and it will erase the drive you just prepared.
sup.41: The ad won't load, or says “try again”
sup.42: This is the single most common report, and it's nearly always the network — not the app. In order of how often it's the fix:
sup.43: Private DNS. Open Settings, search for Private DNS, choose Private DNS provider hostname and enter dns.google. Save, toggle your connection off and on, then restart the app. Ad-blocking DNS providers block the ad servers, so no ad can load.
sup.44: Ad blockers and blocking VPNs. Disable them for the app. There is nothing to load through a blocker.
sup.45: Switch between Wi-Fi and mobile data. If ads load on one and not the other, the network is the cause.
sup.46: Watch the ad to the very end and close it with the X that appears. Pressing Back early cancels the reward.
sup.47: Why does the app need internet just to format a drive?
sup.48: The operation itself doesn't. The connection is for loading ads, which is what funds the free version — the ads are the price of the tools being free.
sup.49: If you want the apps to work fully offline, the one-time Pro upgrade removes ads and the token system entirely, and offline use comes with it.
sup.51: Tap the token counter on the main screen to open Get Tokens. Under Get 1 free token, tap Watch: one video ad of 60 seconds at most gives 1 token. Or buy Get 5 Tokens. Watching is free, up to a balance of 5 tokens and 4 ads each time you open the app.
sup.53: That's a limit, not a bug. Free tokens stop at a balance of 5, and the card then says You have enough tokens. Spend some and Watch comes back. After 4 ads in one session it says No more ads, restart app and try again. Close the app fully and open it again.
sup.55: Most tools are free. Only these cost tokens, and the number is always shown before you confirm:
sup.55a: ISO Burner (Ultimate USB, DROFUS): 2 for a Disk or ISO image copied file by file, such as a Windows ISO; 1 for Non-bootable, MS-DOS or FreeDOS. Images written as an exact copy (Raspberry Pi and other .img files, macOS DMG, and Linux ISOs unless you tick Advanced Options) are free.
sup.55d: Partition Wizard (Ultimate USB, USB Tools): 1 for each Create or Format step, at most 3 per Apply Changes.
sup.55e: PS2 USB Utils (Ultimate USB, USB Tools): 1 when Fix formats the drive.
sup.56: Everything else is free, including Wipe USB, Bad Blocks Check, Benchmark, Backup / Restore, USB Defragmenter, Raw Write, the file managers, Game Converter and adding PS2 games. If an operation fails, or the app closes before it finishes, the tokens are given back.
sup.57: I watched the ad but got no token
sup.58: The reward is granted when the ad reports completion, so it's lost if the ad is closed early or the connection drops mid-ad. Watch to the end, close with the X, and stay connected.
sup.59: If the ad definitely completed and the balance didn't move, force-stop the app (Settings → Apps → the app → Force stop) and reopen it while online.
sup.61: Token balances are stored on your device, not on an account. Uninstalling the app or clearing its data deletes them. They move to a new phone only if Android's own backup or phone transfer brings back the app's data.
sup.62: Pro is different — it's tied to your Google account and survives all of that.
sup.64: What does Pro actually give me?
sup.65: A one-time, lifetime purchase that removes all ads, removes the token system, and lets the app run fully offline and with ad blockers enabled. There is no subscription.
sup.66: To be precise about what it isn't: Pro removes the ads and the token requirement. It isn't a separate feature set — the tools themselves are the same.
sup.67: I bought Pro and it isn't showing
sup.68: Make sure the Play Store on this phone uses the same Google account that made the purchase. The apps have no sign-in of their own.
sup.69: Force-stop the app (Settings → Apps → the app → Force stop), then reopen it while online — the entitlement is confirmed with Google Play on launch.
sup.70: Check the purchase actually completed in the Play Store under Payments & subscriptions.
sup.71: If it still doesn't appear, email us with the Play Store order number.
sup.72: I bought tokens and they didn't arrive
sup.73: Force-stop the app and reopen it while connected — the purchase is verified on launch, so a purchase made while offline or during a dropped connection can land a moment later.
sup.74: If they still aren't there, send us a screenshot of the app and a screenshot of the purchase in your Google Play payment history, and we'll sort it out.
sup.75: Do I keep Pro on a new phone?
sup.76: Yes. Pro follows the Google account, not the device. Install the app on the new phone with the same Google account in the Play Store, and Pro comes back when the app starts. Your token balance stays on the old phone unless Android's own backup or phone transfer brings back the app's data.
sup.77: Do I have to buy Pro separately for each app?
sup.78: Yes. Each app is a separate product on Google Play with its own purchase. If you want everything in one place, Ultimate USB contains the features of the individual tools.
sup.79: I can't complete a purchase in my country
sup.80: In-app purchases go through Google Play billing, and Play payment support varies by country — in some regions purchases are restricted regardless of the app. Nothing on our side can override that.
sup.81: Everything remains usable in the meantime: tokens are earned free by watching a rewarded ad, and no feature is locked behind payment alone.
sup.82: Can I get a discount or promo code?
sup.83: Google Play promo codes can only make an item completely free — there is no mechanism for a partial per-user discount, so we can't issue one.
sup.84: Every paid action is also reachable free by watching a rewarded ad, so nothing is locked behind payment.
sup.85: How do I request a refund?
sup.86: Refunds are processed by Google Play, not by us, so start there: open the Play Store, find the purchase in your order history, and use the option to report a problem with it.
sup.87: If the purchase failed to deliver, email us first with a screenshot of the app and of the Play purchase history — most cases turn out to be recoverable without a refund.
sup.89: No. These apps rely on low-level USB and storage access that iOS doesn't provide. Android only, and a purchase on Android doesn't carry to any other platform.
sup.91: Which file system should I choose?
sup.92: FAT32 — maximum compatibility (TVs, car stereos, consoles, BIOS boot). Single files are limited to 4 GB.
sup.93: exFAT — no practical file-size limit, still read by phones, Windows and macOS. The best default for general use.
sup.94: NTFS — for Windows. No practical file-size limit, but most Android phones can't read it.
sup.95: ext2/3/4 — for Linux. Neither Android nor Windows reads it without extra software.
sup.95b: Ultimate USB and USB Tools offer all of these in Format USB. DROFUS offers FAT32, exFAT and NTFS for a Non-bootable drive, and Ventoy offers FAT32, exFAT and NTFS for its drive.
sup.96: I formatted to NTFS (or ext4) and now my phone can't read the drive
sup.97: The format succeeded. The limitation is Android itself: most Android devices have no built-in NTFS or ext2/3/4 support, so the system can't mount the drive even though a PC will read it perfectly. A handful of manufacturers add NTFS support, but it is the exception rather than the rule.
sup.98: Ultimate USB and Ventoy still open the drive in USB File Manager, because they carry their own drivers for these file systems instead of relying on Android's.
sup.99: If you need the drive readable by the phone's own file manager and other apps, use exFAT. It has no practical file-size limit and is read by Android, Windows and macOS alike.
sup.100: Format failed, or the verification check failed
sup.101: Confirm the adapter is a data OTG adapter and reseat it.
sup.102: Test the drive on a PC — a drive that fails verification usually has failing flash.
sup.103: Try a different USB port on the adapter or a different adapter entirely.
sup.104: In Ultimate USB and USB Tools, run Bad Blocks Check to confirm whether the flash itself is at fault. It erases the drive.
sup.105: A verification failure means data written to the drive read back differently. That is a hardware symptom, and no app can format around it.
sup.106: The drive shows less capacity than it should
sup.107: Two ordinary causes and one bad one:
sup.108: Manufacturers count in decimal gigabytes; your phone counts in binary. A "64 GB" drive genuinely holds about 59 GiB.
sup.109: A previous bootable write may have left hidden partitions. Recover the space with Partition Wizard or Format USB in Ultimate USB and USB Tools, by writing the drive with Non-bootable in DROFUS, or with Clear in Ventoy.
sup.110: If the shortfall is large, the drive may be counterfeit. All four apps test the end of the drive when it is connected and show 🛑 CRITICAL WARNING: BAD DRIVE! if it fails.
sup.111: How do I get back unallocated space?
sup.112: In Ultimate USB and USB Tools, open Partition Wizard, select the unallocated block and tap Create, or Delete the existing partitions and create one across the drive. Your changes are listed for review, then Apply Changes runs them together.
sup.113: The quickest route, if you don't need what's on the drive: Format USB in Ultimate USB and USB Tools, or Non-bootable in DROFUS.
sup.115: GPT for modern UEFI machines. MBR for older BIOS/legacy boot, and for consoles like the PS2 that require it.
sup.116: In Ultimate USB and USB Tools, Partition Wizard converts between them without a PC (Convert Partition Table). In DROFUS and Ventoy you choose the Partition Table: before writing. Back the drive up first regardless — any change to a partition table is a change you don't want to get halfway through.
sup.118: Which app should I use to make a bootable drive?
sup.119: DROFUS — one ISO, maximum control over the result. The straightforward choice for a Windows or Linux installer.
sup.120: Ventoy (Unofficial) — install once, then drag as many ISOs onto the drive as it holds and pick at boot. Best if you carry several installers.
sup.121: Ultimate USB — contains both, plus partitioning, diagnostics and the rest.
sup.122: The drive was created but the PC won't boot from it
sup.123: The write can be perfect and the PC still refuse it. Check, in this order:
sup.124: Boot menu. Actually select the USB drive in the boot menu (usually F12, F11, F9 or Esc at power-on) rather than expecting it to boot on its own.
sup.125: Secure Boot. Disable it in the BIOS/UEFI, or use a build that supports it.
sup.126: Partition scheme. GPT drives need UEFI mode; MBR drives need legacy/CSM. A mismatch means the drive simply won't appear.
sup.127: USB port. Try a rear port directly on the motherboard, not a front-panel or hub port.
sup.128: The ISO itself. Re-download it if it came from anywhere other than the official source — a truncated ISO writes fine and boots into nothing.
sup.129: My Windows ISO has a file bigger than 4 GB
sup.130: That's install.wim, and FAT32 can't hold it. In Ultimate USB and DROFUS, tick Split image for FAT32 compatibility. to split it into .swm parts so the drive can stay FAT32, which modern Secure Boot PCs usually need. Windows setup puts the parts back together; nothing is lost. Splitting takes a long time.
sup.131: Without the tick the app uses NTFS, which has no size limit but isn't accepted by every UEFI firmware. On a Ventoy drive the ISO is copied as one file, so use exFAT or NTFS there.
sup.132: How do I switch Ventoy between MBR and GPT?
sup.133: In Ventoy, or in Ultimate USB under Ventoy - Unofficial, choose MBR or GPT under Partition Table:, then tap Install. You don't need a PC.
sup.134: Install wipes the drive completely, including any ISOs already copied to it, so copy them back afterwards with Copy File To USB. Update keeps your ISOs but doesn't change the partition table.
sup.135: How do I add or remove ISOs on a Ventoy drive?
sup.136: In Ultimate USB and Ventoy, once Ventoy is installed, add ISOs with Copy File To USB, or save them straight to the drive with Download File Directly To USB FROM INTERNET. Copying them on a PC works too. No reburning, no reinstalling. Delete an ISO in USB File Manager and it leaves the boot menu.
sup.137: What is Linux persistence, and why is the option greyed out?
sup.138: Persistence keeps your files and changes on the USB drive across reboots of a live Linux system. In Ultimate USB and DROFUS, tick Advanced Options (Filesystem, Partition & Persistence), then set Persistent partition size. The app adds an ext3 or ext4 partition for it.
sup.139: It's offered only for images that support it. For the others the app says why: the image doesn't support it, the distribution sets it up itself, or the image is written sector by sector. It also needs enough free space on the drive. On a Ventoy drive, use Add persistence in Config Hub (Ultimate USB, Ventoy).
sup.141: In Ultimate USB and DROFUS, choosing Windows To Go instead of Standard Windows Installation puts a full Windows installation on the USB drive itself, rather than an installer for a PC. It can take several hours: use a fast drive, a fast phone and High-speed mode., and start with a full battery.
sup.142: Can I burn a macOS DMG or a Raspberry Pi image?
sup.143: Yes, in Ultimate USB and DROFUS (ISO Burner, Disk or ISO image), with no token cost. macOS DMG (Intel-based), Raspberry Pi OS and other ARM images are written as raw blocks, preserving the original layout and boot structure. There's no customisation applied to these, by design.
sup.145: The operation is stuck or won't finish
sup.146: Three causes cover almost every case:
sup.147: The app was minimised. Operations pause when the app leaves the foreground — that's deliberate, to protect the drive from a half-finished write. Keep it on screen and keep the screen awake.
sup.148: The adapter or drive. Reseat the adapter, don't move the phone while it runs, and try another adapter if it recurs. A loose or charge-only adapter is the usual culprit.
sup.148b: No internet or an ad blocker (free version). The app shows No Internet Connection or Adblocker or Private DNS detected., and running operations wait until that's fixed. Pro doesn't pause for either.
sup.149: Large drives and large images simply take time — a write that looks frozen on a slow drive is often still progressing. If the progress figure hasn't moved at all for a long stretch, treat it as a stall and check the two points above.
sup.150: It stalls near the very end — 99%, or in the last few percent
sup.151: The end of a write is where data reaches the far end of the drive. Stalling there is the classic signature of a drive that reports more capacity than it physically has, or whose flash is failing at the far end.
sup.152: In Ultimate USB and USB Tools, run Bad Blocks Check with Detect fake / counterfeit capacity ticked (it erases the drive). In DROFUS and Ventoy, reconnect the drive: if the end-of-drive test fails, the app shows 🛑 CRITICAL WARNING: BAD DRIVE! and may offer to scan for the size the drive really holds. If the drive is bad, no app can fix it.
sup.153: Can the app damage my USB drive?
sup.154: No. Nothing the app does is unrecoverable at the hardware level — the worst case is a drive that needs formatting again. If a drive stopped working after an operation, it was already failing.
sup.155: Can I use my phone while an operation runs?
sup.156: Not on other apps — operations pause when the app is minimised. Leave it in the foreground until it finishes. Long operations on large drives can take a while, so start them when you don't need the phone.
sup.157: The app crashed or closed by itself
sup.158: First check you installed from Google Play. Modified or repackaged copies from APK sites are a common source of crashes we can't reproduce or fix.
sup.159: If it's the Play version, write to us with the app version, your phone model, the drive size and file system, and what you were doing when it closed. Crashes we can reproduce get fixed quickly.
sup.161: How do I tell if a drive is counterfeit?
sup.162: In Ultimate USB and USB Tools, run Bad Blocks Check with Detect fake / counterfeit capacity ticked. It writes across the whole drive and reads it back, so it erases everything on it. A counterfeit drive reports a large capacity but silently discards anything past its real size, which the test exposes. All four apps also test the end of the drive when it is connected and show 🛑 CRITICAL WARNING: BAD DRIVE! if it fails.
sup.163: Symptoms before you test: files that copy successfully but are corrupt afterwards, and writes that stall near the end.
sup.164: Can a corrupted drive be repaired?
sup.165: Logical corruption, such as a broken partition table or file system, is usually fixed by formatting fresh: Format USB or Wipe USB in Ultimate USB and USB Tools, Non-bootable in DROFUS, or Install in Ventoy. The apps don't repair a drive in place, so copy off what you need first.
sup.166: Physical flash failure isn't repairable by any software. If Bad Blocks Check (Ultimate USB, USB Tools) reports errors, replace the drive.
sup.167: Does Wipe USB really erase everything?
sup.168: Wipe USB (Ultimate USB, USB Tools) overwrites the whole drive once with zeros, which matches the "Clear" level in NIST SP 800-88 and defeats all normal file-recovery software. Choose Sampled (recommended) or Full verification to have it read the drive back, and save the erasure report and certificate when it finishes.
sup.169: It is not a multi-pass or "Purge"-level erase, and we don't claim it is. For legally mandated destruction standards, follow your own policy.
sup.170: My drive is slower than advertised
sup.171: In Ultimate USB and USB Tools, run Benchmark for real numbers. Bear in mind the whole chain limits speed: a USB 3.0 drive in a USB 2.0 adapter runs at USB 2.0 speed, and advertised figures are usually peak read, not sustained write.
sup.172: Small-file writes are always dramatically slower than large sequential ones. That's how flash works, not a fault.
sup.174: How do I set up a drive for PS2 / OPL?
sup.175: In Ultimate USB and USB Tools, open PS2 USB Utils. If the drive isn't FAT32 or exFAT with an MBR partition table, tap Fix to prepare it (1 token, erases the drive). Then add games with Import & Split ISO. On FAT32, games of 4 GB or more are converted to USBExtreme (.ul) and ul.cfg is updated. Other games can use Direct Copy - Recommended.
sup.176: OPL needs unfragmented game files. If a game shows Fragmented, tap Defragment. If that can't finish, use Run Full Defragmenter.
sup.177: Which game formats can be converted?
sup.178: In Ultimate USB and USB Tools, Game Converter converts between ISO, BIN/CUE, VCD, ZSO, CSO and CHD, in the directions each format supports. Compressing to ZSO or CSO saves considerable space at a small performance cost.
sup.179: Do you supply the games, BIOS files, or console firmware?
sup.180: No. The apps are tools for organising files you already own. We don't bundle, host or distribute game images, BIOS files, console firmware or any proprietary console component. PlayStation 1 games on a PS2 drive need a system file in /POPS/ that you must supply yourself.
sup.182: In Ultimate USB and USB Tools, Download Game Arts fetches artwork online, so it needs a working connection. Games with an unusual or renamed game ID may have no artwork available to match.
sup.185: It's been retired. Every feature it had is in DROFUS, along with everything added since — install that instead.
sup.186: Which app do I need if I only want one?
sup.187: Ultimate USB. It contains the bootable-USB writer, Ventoy, formatting, partitioning, diagnostics, backup and the console-game tools in one app. The separate apps exist for people who want just one job done.
sup.188: Do my files get uploaded anywhere?
sup.189: No. Your files are processed on your device, and their contents are never uploaded to us. What each app does send, such as ad requests, crash reports and purchase checks, is set out in that app's own privacy policy; each app links to it in its menu, and all of them are listed on our privacy page.
sup.190: Do the apps create an account?
sup.191: No. There's no sign-up, no profile and no account to delete. Pro is tied to your Google Play purchase, which Google manages, and tokens live on your device.
sup.192: How do I restore a backup, or open a .bk file?
sup.193: In Ultimate USB and USB Tools, open Backup / Restore and tap Restore to write a .bk backup back to a drive. To look inside one without restoring it, open the .bk file in Ultimate USB's Partition Image Manager.
sup.194: Is the app available in my language?
sup.195: The apps are translated into many languages and follow your phone's language setting. If a translation is wrong or missing, send us the screen and the correct wording — corrections from native speakers are genuinely welcome.
sup.196: ChaoMe: my theme won't apply, or resets after a while
sup.197: On recent HyperOS versions, Xiaomi's Themes app checks a theme's rights with Xiaomi's servers and may refuse an edited theme. No app can change that. You can still try single parts under Customize theme in the Themes app, and ChaoMe's Set Wallpaper button applies a theme's wallpaper directly. Where a theme does apply, Xiaomi's rights check usually resets it within a few hours; your edits stay in the .mtz file and you can apply it again.
sup.198: ChaoMe: why does it need Shizuku?
sup.199: From Android 11 onwards, apps can't read or write the Themes app's folder. With Shizuku, ChaoMe lists the themes already on your phone and puts your theme into Themes → My themes. On Android 13 and later, Shizuku started in ADB (wireless debugging) mode can't write there; only Shizuku started with root can. Shizuku is optional: without it, ChaoMe still builds and exports the .mtz file.
sup.201: Message us with the four details above and we'll work through it with you. WhatsApp is quickest for anything involving a screenshot; email is better for purchases and refunds.

sup.ch.1: ChaoMe: which phones and versions are supported?
sup.ch.2: Themes can be built for MIUI 9.4 or earlier, MIUI 9.5 to 11, MIUI 12, 12.5, 13 and 14, and HyperOS 1, 2 and 3. Choose yours under Settings → Phone system version.
sup.ch.3: ChaoMe: what does Theme check do?
sup.ch.4: Theme check reads a theme and lists errors, warnings and store rules from the official theme rules, each with the screen that fixes it. It is advice only and never blocks an export. Open it from its tile in the editor, or from the button after a theme is saved.
sup.ch.5: ChaoMe: where are my themes saved?
sup.ch.6: Exported .mtz files go to MIUI/theme on your phone, or to a folder you choose on the export screen: tick Edit file name or path, clear Use the default path (MIUI/theme) and tap …. Every theme you build is also kept in the Theme library, where you can search, compare two themes, reuse single parts and start from a template. The library lives inside the app, so uninstalling it or clearing its data deletes the library: back it up to a zip file from the library first.
sup.ch.7: ChaoMe: my font doesn't change everywhere
sup.ch.8: A font theme changes only the phone's default font. Other font styles, letters the font doesn't contain, and apps with their own fonts keep their font. Restart the phone after applying the theme to see the new font.
sup.ch.9: ChaoMe: how do I change the app's language?
sup.ch.10: Use Settings → Language. ChaoMe is available in English, Hindi, Indonesian, Russian and Simplified Chinese, and System default follows your phone's language.
sup.ch.11: ChaoMe: what does PRO add, and how do I restore it?
sup.ch.12: PRO removes every ad, lets you use the app offline and unlocks the advanced tools (the advanced editors: file browser, XML editor, raw keys and resource catalogue; lock screen options; the new lock screen with its depth, dark-mode, charging and fingerprint options; always-on display and power menu; MAML code with live preview; combining with parts of other themes; and converting a theme for another system version); every other editor, Theme check, .bak import, sharing and exporting, previews and undo/redo stay free. PRO is a one-time purchase tied to your Google account, and the app reads it from Google Play each time it starts or comes back to the screen, so there is no restore button: reinstall the app or sign in to Google Play with the account that bought it.
sup.ch.13: ChaoMe: how do I change my ad choices?
sup.ch.14: Open Settings → Privacy. Where your region requires it, Ad and data choices reopens the consent form, and in US states with an opt-out right Do not sell or share my personal information stops personalised ads. With PRO, Settings → Privacy shows only the privacy policy. See the ChaoMe privacy policy.
sup.ch.15: ChaoMe: why does the free version need the internet?
sup.ch.16: The free version is supported by ads and needs a connection while it is open. PRO removes ads and works offline. Your themes are always built on your phone and are never uploaded.
sup.ch.17: ChaoMe: I can't see the themes already on my phone
sup.ch.18: Since Android 11, apps can't read the installed-themes folder by themselves. Install Shizuku, start it and tap Allow when ChaoMe asks (on a rooted phone, Shizuku can be started with root). The themes appear the next time ChaoMe starts.
sup.ch.19: ChaoMe: how do I move my theme library to a new phone?
sup.ch.20: In the Theme library, tap Back up to save a zip file, copy it to the new phone and tap Restore there. PRO comes back from Google Play by itself.
sup.fm.1: USB File Manager doesn't see my drive
sup.fm.2: Switch on OTG in your phone's settings if the option exists. Some phones switch it off again after a while.
sup.fm.3: Try another OTG adapter or cable. Charge-only adapters can't carry data.
sup.fm.4: For hard disks, use a powered USB hub: a phone often can't supply enough power on its own.
sup.fm.5: Check the drive on a computer, then unplug it and plug it in again.
sup.fm.6: Android asks to allow access to the USB device
sup.fm.7: Tap Allow. The app can only open the drive after you allow it. If you closed the prompt, tap Allow access on the drive's card, or unplug the drive and plug it in again. If opening fails, tap Try again.
sup.fm.8: Can I write to NTFS drives?
sup.fm.9: Yes, NTFS drives are fully readable and writable. A drive opens read-only only when Windows hibernated it (Fast Startup), when Windows did not close it cleanly and it could not be repaired, or when the drive is write-protected or refuses writes. Shut Windows down fully (not Restart or Sleep), or check the drive in Windows, then connect it again.
sup.fm.10: Copying a file larger than 4 GB fails
sup.fm.11: That is a limit of the FAT32 file system, not of the app: FAT32 can't store a single file over 4 GB. Use a drive formatted as exFAT or NTFS for large files.
sup.fm.12: Can USB File Manager format a drive?
sup.fm.13: No. USB File Manager browses and manages files; it has no formatting, partitioning or disk-image tools. To format, partition or repair a drive, use USB Tools or Ultimate USB.
sup.fm.15: Not for USB drives. Root is only needed for the phone's internal SD card slot, and your root manager (such as Magisk or KernelSU) must allow the app.
sup.fm.16: How do I unplug the drive safely?
sup.fm.17: Wait for any running operation to finish, then tap Eject on the drive's card. When it says Safe to unplug, pull the drive out. If something could not be saved, the app tells you to check the drive on a computer. Unplugging during a copy can damage the files being written.
sup.fm.18: I bought Pro and it isn't active
sup.fm.19: Pro is a one-time purchase tied to your Google account. Open ⋮ → Go Pro: remove ads (or Settings → Remove ads) and tap Restore purchases while online. If it still isn't active, check that the Play Store is signed in with the account that bought it and that the payment isn't still pending. Pro removes all ads, the No Internet Connection pause and the ad-blocker notice, and once confirmed it works offline for up to 30 days at a time.
sup.fm.20: The app says it is out of date
sup.fm.21: When the app shows Update Required, tap UPDATE NOW to open its Google Play page. If the update isn't mandatory you can tap LATER. If it is, there is no LATER button and the app closes after a few seconds until it is updated.
sup.fm.22: Which file systems and drives work?
sup.fm.23: FAT12, FAT16, FAT32, exFAT, NTFS and ext2/3/4, all readable and writable, on flash drives, card readers, hard disks and SSDs (through a powered hub if needed). Drives with several partitions (MBR or GPT) show each one by its label, or as Partition 1, Partition 2 and so on when it has none, and you can open several drives and partitions at once in tabs.
sup.fm.24: The app warns that my drive may store less than its size says
sup.fm.25: That is typical of counterfeit drives, which report more space than they really have. Files written beyond the real capacity can be lost, so don't keep your only copy of important files on that drive.
sup.fm.26: How do I change my ad choices in USB File Manager?
sup.fm.27: Where your region requires it, open ⋮ → Settings → Help & about → Privacy Settings to reopen the consent form. Pro has no ads at all. See the USB File Manager privacy policy.
sup.fm.28: It says an ad blocker was detected
sup.fm.29: While an operation runs, the free version pauses if ads are blocked by an ad-blocker app, Private DNS or your network. Turn the blocker off, or set Private DNS to dns.google, then restart the app. Pro works with ad blockers.
sup.fm.30: How do I open or share a file with another app?
sup.fm.31: Tap the file, or use Open with… or Share (up to 16 files). The file is read straight from the drive. With Open with… the app you choose can also save changes back to it; a shared file can only be read.
sup.fm.32: How do I copy files between my phone and the drive?
sup.fm.33: In a folder, tap Add → Import File / Files or Import Directory. To copy to the phone, select files and use Copy to… or Export. The phone side always goes through Android's folder picker.
sup.fm.34: How do I clear the Recent list or rename my drive?
sup.fm.35: Recent tab → Clear history; the list stays on your phone and is not backed up. To rename a drive, open it and use ⋮ → Rename label.

sup.tt.1: Is TumTum free? Are there in-app purchases?
sup.tt.2: TumTum is free and supported by ads, and it has no in-app purchases. Every level is unlocked simply by playing.
sup.tt.3: How do I get coins and hints?
sup.tt.4: You earn coins by solving levels for the first time (more for more stars and for 3-star streaks) and from a chest at the end of every fifth chapter. A hint costs 10 coins. If you tap Hint without enough coins and a video is available, you can choose Watch an ad to earn 15 coins. Watching is always optional.
sup.tt.6: Every level is checked by a solver to make sure it has a solution, and the move limit is based on the best one. One swipe moves every character until it hits something, so the order of your swipes matters. Pits and spikes are one-way, and only Undo brings a character back. Use Undo or Restart freely, or tap Hint.
sup.tt.8: Yes. Every level plays fully offline. Ads and the optional videos for extra coins need a connection.
sup.tt.9: My progress is gone, or I changed phones
sup.tt.10: Progress, stars and coins are saved on your device. There is no account and no cloud save, so clearing the game's data or uninstalling it resets your progress. If Android backup is on, reinstalling on the same phone may bring it back, but progress can't be moved to a different phone model.
sup.tt.11: How do I turn off personalized ads or crash reports?
sup.tt.12: Open Settings → Privacy in the game. Tap Personalised ads • On to turn personalisation off (with US English it's shown as Do not sell or share my personal information). Where your region requires it, Ad and data choices reopens the consent form. Switch Crash reports off or on there too. See the TumTum privacy policy for the details.
sup.tt.13: Why don't I see the “Watch an ad” option?
sup.tt.14: It appears only when you tap Hint without enough coins and a video has loaded. You need a connection, and in regions that require consent, ads stay off until you answer the privacy prompt. You can change your answer in Settings → Privacy → Ad and data choices.
sup.tt.15: How do I turn off sound, music or vibration?
sup.tt.16: Open Settings → Sound & vibration in the game. Sound, music and vibration each have their own switch, and sound and music have a volume slider.
sup.tt.17: Can I change the game's language?
sup.tt.18: Yes. TumTum is available in 11 languages and follows your phone's language by default. To choose another, open Settings → Language in the game; pick System default to follow the phone again.
sup.tt.19: Does TumTum need an account or upload anything?
sup.tt.20: No. There's no account or sign-up, and the game handles none of your files. It sends only ad requests and, if switched on, crash reports. See the TumTum privacy policy.
sup.u.1: Do I lose tokens if an operation fails?
sup.u.2: No. If an operation fails, or the app closes before it finishes, the tokens it cost are given back, at the latest the next time you open the app.
sup.u.3: Why did everything pause with “No Internet Connection”?
sup.u.4: The free version needs a connection for its ads. While you're offline it shows No Internet Connection, and running operations wait. Nothing is lost: they continue on their own once you're back online. Pro works fully offline.
sup.u.5: It says “Adblocker or Private DNS detected.”
sup.u.6: The free version can't load ads through an ad blocker, a blocking VPN or ad-blocking Private DNS. Running operations wait until it's switched off for the app. Set Private DNS to dns.google or turn it off, then restart the app. Pro, or any token pack you've bought on this install, lets the app run with an ad blocker on.
sup.u.7: Why does it ask me to solve a sum before buying?
sup.u.8: That's Parental Verification. If Google Play reports that the account belongs to a teenager, a purchase needs a parent's check first. For younger users, and for supervised accounts whose approval is pending or was declined, purchases are off.
sup.u.9: How do I change my ad and privacy choices?
sup.u.10: Tap the ? (Help) button on the main screen. Where your region requires it, Privacy Settings reopens the consent form, where you can change or withdraw consent and, in US states with an opt-out right, opt out of the sale or sharing of your data. Privacy Policy in the same menu opens the app's policy: Ultimate USB, DROFUS, Ventoy, USB Tools. Pro shows no ads at all.
sup.u.11: Can other apps open the files on my USB drive?
sup.u.12: In Ultimate USB, Partition Mounter mounts a partition as Read Only or Read / Write; tap Open Files App and other apps can open it through Android's file picker. Unmount it before unplugging. In Ultimate USB and Ventoy, opening a file in USB File Manager lets you choose another app to open it straight from the drive.
sup.u.13: Can I work on a disk image file instead of a drive?
sup.u.14: In Ultimate USB, Partition Image Manager opens or creates a partition image file (Create Partition Image .img) and lets you browse and edit it like a drive. Raw Write writes an image file to a drive byte by byte. DROFUS, Ventoy and USB Tools work on drives only.
sup.u.15: I forgot the password of an encrypted drive
sup.u.16: It can't be recovered or reset; that's what protects the files. In Ultimate USB, USB Encryption can only make the drive usable again by formatting it, which erases everything. While you still know the password, Change Password changes it quickly.
sup.u.17: How do I use the phone's SD card slot?
sup.u.18: It needs a rooted phone. Choose SD Slot instead of USB OTG on the main screen, tap Grant and accept your root manager's prompt, then Mount. Without root, put the card in a USB card reader and use USB OTG.
sup.u.19: What does “CRITICAL WARNING: BAD DRIVE!” mean?
sup.u.20: When a drive is connected, the app writes a test pattern near its end and reads it back. If that fails, the drive is faulty, the cable is loose, or the drive is counterfeit and smaller than it claims, and a write is likely to fail. If the app offers to scan for the real size, tap Yes to use only the part that works, or try another cable or drive.
sup.u.21: What do the Windows setup options do?
sup.u.22: In Ultimate USB and DROFUS, Windows Setup Customization changes the installer you write. It can remove the TPM 2.0, Secure Boot and 4 GB RAM checks, drop the online Microsoft account requirement, create a local account (Windows asks for its password at first sign-in), skip the privacy questions, copy regional settings from your phone and turn off automatic BitLocker encryption. Nothing you enter leaves the phone. On a Ventoy drive, Config Hub has Windows 11: bypass hardware checks and Windows 11: bypass online account instead.
sup.u.23: Can I theme or password-protect a Ventoy drive?
sup.u.24: Yes, in Ultimate USB and Ventoy. Theme Manager imports a GRUB2 theme archive onto the drive, and Get more themes opens a theme website in your browser. Config Hub sets a boot-menu password, menu options and persistence. These settings are written only to the drive.
sup.u.25: How do I get an erasure certificate?
sup.u.26: In Ultimate USB and USB Tools, run Wipe USB. When it finishes, tap View erasure report or View erasure certificate and save it. It can't be produced again later. The certificate is made on your phone and goes nowhere unless you share it.
